HON. NOAH AHMED — EMPOWERING THE GEN Z GENERATION

Hon. Noah Ahmed’s proposed vision for young people is built on one fundamental principle: young people should not only be the leaders of tomorrow—they should have meaningful opportunities to contribute today.

His youth empowerment agenda would focus on turning the energy, creativity and innovation of Gen Z into skills, businesses, employment and sustainable livelihoods across Taraba State.

Under this proposed vision, youth development would include:

💡 TECHNOLOGY & DIGITAL SKILLS
Create opportunities for young people to learn AI, cybersecurity, software development, digital marketing, graphics, content creation and other emerging technologies.

🚀 STARTUP & BUSINESS SPONSORSHIP
Support promising youth-owned businesses through transparent grants, equipment, mentorship and access to business development programmes—not just one-time handouts.

🎓 EDUCATION & SCHOLARSHIPS
Expand opportunities for scholarships, vocational training, professional certifications and technical education so that financial hardship does not prevent talented young people from developing their potential.

🎨 CREATIVE INDUSTRY SUPPORT
Provide structured support for musicians, filmmakers, photographers, designers, writers, fashion entrepreneurs and other creatives through training, sponsorship and platforms for showcasing their work.

⚽ SPORTS DEVELOPMENT
Invest in grassroots sports by supporting young athletes, coaches and sporting programmes, while creating pathways for talented youths to compete at higher levels.

💼 JOBS, INTERNSHIPS & ENTREPRENEURSHIP
Build partnerships with private businesses and institutions to create internships, apprenticeships and employment opportunities while helping young entrepreneurs develop sustainable enterprises.

🏢 YOUTH INNOVATION CENTRES
Develop spaces where young people can access training, internet connectivity, mentorship, technology and collaborative opportunities.

A NEW APPROACH TO YOUTH SPONSORSHIP

The goal should be to move from “giving young people something” to “giving young people the tools to build something.”

Every sponsorship programme should be transparent, merit-based and accessible to young people across communities and local government areas.

HON. NOAH AHMED’S MESSAGE TO THE GEN Z GENERATION:

> “Your ideas matter. Your talent matters. Your future matters. Government should create an environment where a young person with an idea, skill or dream has a genuine opportunity to turn that potential into reality.”

Empower the youth. Invest in talent. Sponsor innovation. Create opportunity. Build a stronger Taraba.

AI IS CHANGING FASHION, AND IT’S BIGGER THAN IMAGE GENERATION.🧵

Artificial Intelligence is quietly transforming almost every stage of the fashion value chain.

From design and trend forecasting to marketing, production, e-commerce, and customer experience, AI is changing how fashion businesses operate.

🧵Here are a few areas where the impact is already visible:

🔹 Design & Ideation:- Exploring silhouettes, patterns, colors, and collection concepts faster.

🔹 Trend Forecasting:-  Using data to identify emerging consumer preferences and market trends.

🔹 Virtual Prototyping:-  Visualizing designs before spending heavily on materials and production.

🔹 Personalization:- Helping brands recommend products and experiences based on customer preferences.

🔹 Marketing & Content:-  Accelerating campaign concepts, storytelling, product descriptions, and visual development.

🔹 Demand Forecasting:- Helping brands make smarter production and inventory decisions, potentially reducing waste.

But here’s what I find most interesting:

AI may not replace the fashion designer. It may replace some of the limitations that slow the designer down.

Creativity still requires taste.

Culture still requires understanding.

Craftsmanship still requires skill.

And strategy still requires human judgment.

For African fashion, this presents an even bigger opportunity.

Imagine combining African heritage, traditional craftsmanship, modern design thinking, and AI-powered innovation to build globally competitive fashion brands.

The question is no longer:

“Will AI affect fashion?”

It already is.

The better question is:

👉🏼How will fashion entrepreneurs use AI to build better brands, products, and businesses?”

This Paper is one of the cleverest solutions I’ve seen for fixing Diffusion Alignment.

If you’ve worked with RLHF or Reward Backprop on DiTs, you must be tired of delayed feedback. 

Evaluating only the final image makes credit assignment a total nightmare. 

You either run out of VRAM trying to unroll the full trajectory, or you fight insane gradient variance with online RL.

The authors solve this by sticking learnable, position-free "register tokens" into a frozen DiT. 

Instead of waiting until step 50, these registers pull dense reward signals directly out of noisy intermediate latents. 

It turns out you can accurately judge trajectory quality surprisingly early in the denoising process.

What makes this paper stand out is how practical the applications are:

1-For training: Their distillation setup (RG-OPD) skips standard policy gradients entirely and hits the same alignment performance while using up to 33x fewer GPU hours. That’s huge for making alignment accessible.

2-For inference: You can use their Reward-Guided Sampling (RGS) to steer generation live off these register gradients thus improving both prompt adherence and visual quality without retraining or touching model weights.

It’s a super clean, well thought-out approach that addresses both the compute bottleneck and inference control at once. 

Definitely worth a read if you're working on generative models:
https://t.co/tfkSPmYwiU

Using text prompts to generate an image of a person on a computer is easy. Generating one with two people is similarly simple. But creating an image of multiple people actually doing something, and faithfully reproducing not just the people but that thing they're all doing? Not so easy.
 
Now, a Cornell research group has devised a way to do just that, incorporating the poses of all individuals in an image to inform the generation, making the scene more believable and accurate.
